decisions.title: Measured feedback and lifecycle commands own the live plant
decisions.detail: R235 makes MuJoCo qpos/qvel/root the only live-plant state source for the persistent 50 Hz Rust WBC. Green TARGET remains a state-local preview query; orange Ctrl-drag is an expiring world-frame external wrench. plant_pause releases the wrench, freezes MuJoCo time, skips WBC/physics, and keeps a heartbeat; plant_resume restarts from the frozen measured state without restoring the old wrench; plant_reset clears the wrench, rebuilds balanced standing, increments reset_epoch, and preserves paused ownership. Worker, protocol, UI-contract, and Rust server tests cover freeze/heartbeat, resume, reset-while-paused, and paused-load rejection. This admits ownership and fail-safe lifecycle semantics, not green-target realization or a recovery policy.

decisions.title: Measured MuJoCo ground and collision state are distinct from preview intent
decisions.detail: R234 constructs the filled grid from MuJoCo's streamed plane point/normal and overlays its collision geometry, CoM projection, contacts, and constraint witnesses in orange while green remains a non-plant WBC query. The one-metre-down preview retains 0.250000 mm collision and 0.162025 mm exact visual clearance. The expanded 250/50 Hz gateway passes contact/load, finite-vector, command expiry, fall/reset/recovery, and reconnect tests on the existing single port-8777 service. This admits observability and state ownership only, not green-target plant realization.

decisions.title: Fresh RK4 laws retain the mechanism but reject transferable final-tangent accuracy
decisions.detail: R233 freezes R232's 64 sweeps before generating two unused RK4 law/state families. Direct returned-tangent scoring gives medium/elliptic 46/48 frozen coverage and 47/48 exact active sets; hard/pyramidal gives 44/48 and 44/48. Both preserve bitwise repeat, zero timed Rust allocation, and the 5 ms deadline at 3.32–3.38 ms p99. Fitted joint widths are 10.446 and 11.248 rad/s, close to but outside the 10 rad/s useful gate. No R224 selection, plant non-regression, or authority follows a failed holdout.

decisions.title: Generalized RK4 work is selected from prediction refinement only
decisions.detail: R232 converts the initial free acceleration to a held generalized force and evaluates four stage-local floating state/contact derivatives with refreshed geometry, bias/inverse dynamics, mass factor, Delassus response, point motion, and collision membership. Classical weights advance pose, tangent, and impulse. The 32→64 prediction change misses the predeclared 2% gate at 2.496%; 64→128 is 0.600%, freezing 64 sweeps at 4.34 ms p99 with repeat and zero allocation. Completed R231 labels are inaccessible until after selection. Its later spent score compares returned and reference final tangents directly: 46/48 coverage and 8.262 rad/s fitted joint width versus 28.584 for the obsolete initial-response proxy.

decisions.title: Fresh RK4 evidence rejects the Euler-family model-coupled profile
decisions.detail: R231 preserves R230's five 1 ms state/event ticks, one compliant update per tick, 32 sweeps, sphere support geometry, and frozen 0.168/0.023/9.893 width. Medium/pyramidal/implicit-fast retains 48/48 exact active sets but covers 47/48. Hard/elliptic/RK4 covers only 24/48, misses 22 actual contact points, and needs 1.894/0.247/62.325 fitted width. Both meet deadline, repeat, and allocation gates. Retain the generic model-owned mechanism, reject the profile, and implement genuine generalized RK4 stages before another holdout.

decisions.title: Model-owned Euler contact evolution is selected without completed labels
decisions.detail: R230 owns floating state, five authored collision ticks, sphere support radius, refreshed point geometry/velocity/convective acceleration, floating inverse dynamics, full Delassus response, and evolved state output in allocation-free Rust. Prediction-only double-sweep convergence selects 32 sweeps at 1.619% of the useful-width gate and about 0.70 ms p99. Only afterward, spent R228 labels show 48/48 exact stiff active sets and fitted combined width 0.168/0.023/9.893. This froze a holdout profile, never authority.

decisions.title: Stiff-contact misses require an evolving coupled re-solve, not a threshold
decisions.detail: R229 explicitly reads the spent R228 labels and cannot promote a profile or authority. Predicted-only foot points occur in every stiff miss but also in covered soft/stiff rows. Their impulse magnitude separates this corpus, but an oracle label mask repairs only four of six misses and sharply worsens the two multi-contact cases. A separately frozen, label-free first ballistic cohort uses the authored five 1 ms ticks and exactly identifies 5/6 initial sets without false points; later contact growth still requires advancing state and re-solving geometry, velocity, and full Delassus response.

decisions.title: Fresh stiff-contact evidence rejects the frozen coupled profile
decisions.detail: R228 keeps R227's 32×32 work, label-free momentum cap, and frozen 0.449/0.065/9.320 width unchanged. Soft/pyramidal/Euler covers 48/48, while stiff/elliptic/implicit-fast covers 42/48 and 98.9943% of components. All six misses predict additional near-simultaneous foot points absent from measured reference load; fitting them would require 1.926/0.338/46.976 width. Query p99 is 0.612/0.418 ms, and repeat, allocation, and exact replay pass, but strict coverage is conjunctive. Retain the generic mechanism; do not tune the misses back into it; admit no selector or authority.

decisions.title: Coupled contact work is selected from causal convergence, not completed labels
decisions.detail: R227 freezes 32 microsteps × 32 forward/reverse projected sweeps. The least-work selection uses only prediction differences and timing: doubling sweeps changes at most 1.200% of the useful-width gate, doubling substeps 16.858%, and worst-law p99 is 0.637 ms under the explicit 5 ms gate. Rejected R221 labels are scored only after selection and cover 48/48 + 48/48 at useful width. This freezes a construction profile for a new holdout; it does not promote a selector, plant action, or authority.

decisions.title: Complete-Delassus positive reference distribution closes the construction gap
decisions.detail: R226 replaces constant-impedance/reference scaling with documented positive K/B, position-dependent impedance, refsafe clamping, declared cone geometry, typed causal free acceleration, and fixed-work complete-Delassus distribution. Six coupled rows cover both rejected R221 laws at useful width and below the explicit 5 ms CPU gate. The representative 32-step/free-acceleration row covers 48/48 + 48/48 at 0.095/0.030/6.131 and 0.449/0.065/9.320 fitted width, with 0.463/0.634 ms p99, bitwise repeat, and zero timed allocation. Retain both generic mechanisms; independently freeze a profile before new evidence, spend no fresh holdout yet, and admit no selector or authority.

decisions.title: External command, impact evidence, and model reserve have distinct provenance
decisions.detail: R225 adds an allocation-free generic Rust contract and /plant-ws protocol 2. Only interactive_operator or evaluation_harness records with declared_continuous_wrench class and world force/application-point frames may execute. Missing provenance, measured_impact_impulse, and unobserved_model_reserve command attempts are rejected before worker mutation; Python independently revalidates accepted records, and measured state echoes their exact source. The public Cloudflare audit passes with stream survival, normal release, and zero MuJoCo warnings. This admits provenance semantics only, not authentication, impact estimation, reserve calibration, safety, or broader authority.

decisions.title: Terminal consequence is now bounded over the full declared velocity box
decisions.detail: R224 propagates every velocity in a componentwise box through the existing ballistic terminal proxy with conservative interval arithmetic. The R222 center score's 7/1 mid/hard false-safe crossings become 0/0, and every contained completed state is bounded with zero timed Rust allocation at 1.388/1.439 µs p99. This retains the generic mechanism only: source coverage remains 91.667%/64.583%, contact-only terminal-projection coverage is 91.667%/39.583%, and the wide box rejects 10/48 and 2/48 safe states. Profile, selection, and authority remain rejected pending a tighter transferable set and plant non-regression.

decisions.title: Terminally scoring only the transition-tube center is false-safe
decisions.detail: R222 scores paired R221 predicted/oracle contact-only states through a generic Rust ballistic terminal proxy with zero physics, policy, controller, or integration. The rejected predictor is optimistic on 33/48 mid-law and 34/48 hard-law samples, producing 7/1 false-safe harm crossings and 5/2 limiting-pressure changes. All eight false-safe rows remain inside R220's componentwise velocity tube. Pair scoring is 0.976/0.816 µs p99, bitwise and allocation-free. Retain generic scoring; require full interval propagation before terminal selection or plant action.

decisions.title: Useful substepped-compliance width does not transfer unchanged across fresh laws
decisions.detail: R221 freezes R220's 128 microsteps, effective-mass/relaxation/impedance mapping, 16× cap scale, and 1.748/0.299/9.802 residual width before untouched offsets 70,000/80,000. Mid/elliptic/implicit-fast covers 44/48 samples and 99.7126% of components; hard/pyramidal/RK4 covers 31/48 and 98.1322%. Every query repeats bitwise, allocates nothing, and remains at 52.646/53.573 µs p99. Strict transfer fails, so the mechanism stays while profile and authority are rejected without holdout tuning.

decisions.title: Stateful compliant evolution is fast and useful on construction labels
decisions.detail: R220 carries signed gap/velocity through explicit Kelvin–Voigt/Coulomb microsteps, full Delassus coupling, and post-impulse gap evolution in allocation-free Rust. The construction-selected 128-step row covers 96/96 immutable R218 samples with a fitted 1.748/0.299/9.802 group box and 55.705 µs p99 query. The mapping, cap scale, step count, and box use source-label knowledge and are not authority; R221 independently rejects their transfer.

decisions.title: Finite estimator-hypothesis expansion fails coverage, width, and deadline together
decisions.detail: R219 types an explicit finite contact set in Rust and envelopes generalized velocity over shared state-local Delassus/response with caller-owned scratch. Atomicity, independent solves, repeat, and zero allocation pass. On immutable R218 labels, 59 scenarios reach 72.917% strict coverage at 7.185 rad/s joint p95 width. Adding all 2⁸ normal-error signs reaches 81.25% at 9.185; larger uncertainty reaches 92.708% at 23.306. Cap inflation reaches 96.875% near 22.5, still misses, and every 315-row p99 exceeds 5 ms (6.383–7.784 ms). The mechanism stays; no construction row earns a holdout or authority.

decisions.title: The frozen coupled contact calibration does not transfer at useful width
decisions.detail: R218 freezes R217's full eight-point Delassus solve, 16 projection sweeps, relaxation mapping, and split root/articulated coefficients before generating 48 soft/pyramidal/Euler and 48 stiff/elliptic/RK4 reset transitions at untouched offsets. Both laws reach 100% sample/component coverage, bitwise repeat, and zero timed Rust allocation. Frozen p95 widths are 2.420/0.142/35.754 and 13.170/0.785/175.201 against 2.0/0.5/10.0 gates; the stiff predictor itself forces at least 17.498 rad/s joint width. No holdout miss is tuned back into the profile. Generic mechanism stays; calibration and authority are rejected.

decisions.title: Coupled contact-law realization is generic Rust machinery, not authority
decisions.detail: R217 exposes the existing allocation-free projected contact solve through ContactTransitionModelSession for arbitrary configured contact counts. Eight G1 prospective points share the full Delassus operator; end-step normal violation, nonnegative normal impulse, circular Coulomb projection, declared restitution and diagonal regularization are explicit. On immutable R215 construction labels it lowers compliant joint residual to 1.521 rad/s p95, but rigid remains 11.277 and the all-label profile remains rejected. R218 independently retains only the mechanism.

decisions.title: Split kinetic geometry cannot rescue an inaccurate causal contact-law/CoP predictor
decisions.detail: R216 replays 96 immutable R215 samples with zero physics, policy, controller or integration steps. The allocation-free Rust split-ellipsoid support matches an independent block inverse and an all-label affine severity envelope covers 96/96 construction samples. Width is still 15.890/0.994/141.487. More fundamentally, the rigid-law causal center predictor has 11.075 rad/s joint p95 residual, forcing at least 22.151 rad/s centered-interval width before residual geometry is chosen; the exact completed-point oracle is only 1.775. Split machinery stays; predictor, fitted profile and authority are rejected.

decisions.title: Finite-patch coupling is physical but full corner uncertainty is still unusable
decisions.detail: R215 replaces four independent point boxes per foot with one resultant spatial-wrench set. Tangent, CoP and torsional capacities share the same nonnegative normal impulse, and the exact allocation-free support checks both passive-slip saturation kinks. On 96 fresh reset G1 transitions, compliant/elliptic/RK4 covers 48/48 while rigid/elliptic/implicit covers 40/48 and 98.9943% of components. P95 widths remain 3.529/0.655/878.035 and 3.180/0.634/923.910 versus 2.0/0.5/10.0 gates; worst-law p99 is 3.410 µs with zero allocation. Mechanism stays; the frozen profile and authority are rejected.

decisions.title: Kinetic impulse geometry is materially narrower but one scalar energy budget is not strict
decisions.detail: R214 implements pᵀM⁻¹p≤E₂ in allocation-free Rust and freezes E₂=f²m(gΔt)² at f=0.50 before two fresh G1 state/law sequences. Exact component support cuts p95 width to 1.092 rad/s root angular, 0.075 m/s root linear and 19.966 rad/s joints. Medium/pyramidal/implicit covers 48/48; hard/pyramidal/Euler covers 47/48 and misses left_ankle_roll_joint at state 20,020. Root gates pass, the 10 rad/s joint gate and strict coverage fail. The primitive is retained; the scalar profile and authority are rejected without holdout tuning.

decisions.title: Independent point boxes do not transfer at useful G1 width
decisions.detail: R213 applies R212's unchanged 50/10/50 continuous-acceleration reserve and R204 directional profile to 96 reset G1 transitions under soft/pyramidal and stiff/elliptic laws. Both laws reach 100% sample/component coverage, but eight independent contact boxes compound through the leg Jacobians to 6.660/1.043/1383.925 root-angular/root-linear/joint p95 widths versus frozen 2.0/0.5/10.0 gates. The generic Rust bound is allocation-free at 2.486 µs worst-law p99. Mechanism stays; profile and authority are rejected.

decisions.title: A grouped continuous-acceleration set closes the immutable Upkie corpus
decisions.detail: R212 performs zero physics, policy, and controller steps and reruns only the Rust directional bound. The 50/10/50 grouped reserve covers 266/266 retained and 8/8 fresh samples at 10.137/1.041/58.020 p95 width; the R204 baseline is bitwise identical and the primary p99 is 0.491 µs with zero allocation. Because the profile was assembled with knowledge of Upkie calibration labels, it is frozen construction evidence for R213, not authority.

decisions.title: Generalized-momentum model queries are generic across Upkie and G1
decisions.detail: R211 introduces generic ContactTransitionModelSession with construction-time frame resolution and preallocated point, spatial, dynamics, and solve scratch. Across 64 pinned-Upkie and 64 pinned-G1 states, Rust singleton/box M⁻¹ projection and three-candidate MΔv residuals agree with independently assembled Pinocchio 4.0 floating mass matrices to 2.984e-13 maximum absolute error. Upkie/G1 box p99 are 8.781/77.813 µs and residual p99 are 6.500/52.119 µs with zero timed allocation and zero policy, controller, integration, or physics steps. This admits model machinery only, not residual/contact authority.

decisions.title: Exact contact labels do not rescue an unconditioned momentum residual
decisions.detail: R210 grants the residual layer the exact completed R206 spatial-wrench response before leave-one-named-case-out calibration. The signed coordinate box reaches 99.624% retained / 100% fresh and keeps joint width at 50.823 rad/s p95, but still misses one right-wheel component and widens root angular/linear response to 28.683 rad/s / 3.370 m/s. A group-symmetric box reaches strict coverage only at 45.463/5.384/584.787. Neither passes the frozen R204 width gate; exact wrench and candidate labels remain evaluation-only.

decisions.title: Label-fit generalized-momentum boxes are not command authority
decisions.detail: R209 retains an allocation-free Rust covector→tangent primitive: M(q)(Δv_observed−Δv_predicted) is boxed in generalized momentum and mapped through exact full M⁻¹. The immutable replay performs zero physics and zero policy steps. All four profiles cover 100% of eight fresh samples but only 98.872% of 266 retained samples. The narrowest p95 widths are 49.056 rad/s root angular, 5.691 m/s root linear, and 179.104 rad/s joint, while a 1.25× expansion closes no additional complete sample. Nearest-candidate fitting is oracle-labelled and all-candidate fitting is wider. Mechanism yes; empirical authority no.

decisions.title: Physical contact-impulse outer bound is admitted as a mechanism, not command authority
decisions.detail: R201 implements Jn,max = meff,max(1+e_max)vclose,max + Fn,maxΔtmax and a friction-cone outer box in allocation-free Rust, with caller-owned M⁻¹Jᵀ projection. Every one of 266 measured intervals is impulse-covered across six declared profiles. The tight row reaches 0.703 N·s p95 at 18.0% utilization; the primary uncertainty row reaches 6.042 N·s at 1.7% and 0.148 µs Rust p99. Model-owned response, full velocity-jump coverage, usefulness, consequence and timing remain mandatory before selection authority.

decisions.title: Exact current contact prestate does not expose a future within-step impact
decisions.detail: R200 appends per-wheel exact pre-solve MuJoCo contact availability, signed distance, and signed constraint-coordinate relative velocity to the frozen R196 causal state feature. Across the same 266 strict leave-one-named-case-out samples, linear/log kNN coverage is 84.962% versus the 85.338% baseline; Lipschitz stays 91.353%, misses by 15.086, and grows to a 39,751.621 p95 bound. Nineteen queries are in flight, and the dominant flight→double→right transition begins after selection. The simulator field is only a candidate-sensor oracle and no residual or authority is admitted.

decisions.title: Existing causal state/model features do not form a useful impulse-transition tube
decisions.detail: R199 predicts normal/tangential impulse and two velocity-jump residuals from current root twist, joint state, selected action, and four-support acceleration center/spread. Strict leave-one-case-out global maxima cover 99.624% only with about 72 rad/s velocity-jump allowance and still miss the left transition; a 25% reserve still misses normal impulse. kNN covers 75.564%, Lipschitz 90.602%, and even physical-support/action oracle grouping 93.609%. No empirical bound is admitted.

decisions.title: Previous-interval contact impulse is not a conservative next-transition state
decisions.detail: R198 adds causal lagged normal, tangential and generalized constraint impulse to the frozen R196 state feature under linear and log scaling. Strict held-out kNN remains 85.338% and Lipschitz remains 91.353%; no sample-coverage gain occurs, while maximum exceedance worsens to 16.151. The strong same-interval R197 correlation is impact-local and cannot be shifted backward into authority.

decisions.title: Tangential contact impulse, not support identity, dominates the remaining realization residual
decisions.detail: R197 adds opt-in plant-only impulse witnesses across all five MuJoCo substeps. Measured physical support is the best rigid qdd hypothesis on 91.35% of 266 selections, yet the four-mode qdd box covers 0/266 realized intervals. Best-mode qdd error reaches 14,718.472 and correlates +0.907 with tangential wheel impulse. Because the impulse is known only after the interval, this localizes the source but cannot authorize a command or serve as a causal bound.

decisions.title: Smooth state-conditioned acceleration residuals do not bound contact-impact tails
decisions.detail: R196 applies strict leave-one-named-case-out evaluation to global, fixed-reserve, action, state-neighbour, Lipschitz, and oracle physical-support/action residual bounds. The closest deployable global maximum covers 99.248% of samples but already needs a 267.523 pressure bound; a declared 25% reserve still misses. kNN covers 85.338%, while Lipschitz covers 91.353% with a 37,977.373 p95 bound. The worst held-out sample crosses flight→double→right contact and has 14,732.8 rad/s² acceleration-model error. No residual enters authority; contact impulse or momentum must be modeled explicitly.

decisions.title: Enumerating support modes does not bound plant realization error
decisions.detail: R195 realizes all three typed efforts under explicit none/left/right/double support, aggregates their Rust terminal scores componentwise, and retains invalid hypotheses as a fail-closed zero-effort outcome. Mechanism gates pass across 270 attempts and 266 valid selections, but the selected envelope covers only 23/266 following-5 ms plant intervals (8.65%); maximum pressure exceedance is 267.523 and the measured-support hypothesis itself misses by a 271.247 pressure-error norm. Handle/5 ms falls 1.245 s before exact control and the synchronous run misses 70 deadlines. The hypothesis set remains visible diagnostic evidence, not authority.

decisions.title: Unavailable contact observation cannot be collapsed to a no-contact zero-effort prediction
decisions.detail: R194 measures 179 executed-withhold intervals and rescales realized 5 ms acceleration through the same terminal scorer. Physical support is double on 169 samples even though the observation is unavailable. Pressure-error norm reaches 28.200; leave-one-case-out coverage falls to 93.3% mirrored-right and 86.4% handle, with a 20.831 worst pressure-bound exceedance. The no-contact model remains a valid named hypothesis, not a conservative singleton. Support-hypothesis aggregation must stay visible and diagnostic until plant bracketing passes.

decisions.title: Correct zero-effort dynamics expose componentwise non-regression as the wrong terminal ordering
decisions.detail: R193 replaces the fictitious zero-qdd withhold baseline with an independently admitted no-contact fixed-zero-effort dynamics witness. All 259 query/replay/causal/allocation gates pass and green sagittal cases survive. Plant consequence still rejects: handle/5 ms moves to 3.055 s, 1.575 s earlier than exact control and 2.915 s earlier than r191. At its first changed choice, support-free would reduce joint-velocity pressure 2.472→0.000, but its tilt pressure 0.862 exceeds the corrected baseline's 0.781, so the Pareto veto changes support-free→withhold. The corrected model stays; the universal componentwise chooser does not gain authority.

decisions.title: A global per-action qdd realization envelope does not survive named-case holdout
decisions.detail: R192 compares each selected r191 candidate's exact roll/pitch and six-joint qdd with measured 5 ms plant-interval acceleration. All 481 samples are finite; withhold/retained/support-free contribute 337/20/124 samples across all seven cases with zero Rust allocation/Python GC. Leave-one-case-out componentwise maxima cover 96.881% of complete samples, and a 5% reserve covers only 97.089%; the worst miss remains 25.234×. These bounds cannot enter terminal authority. State/contact/direction-conditioned realization or a different candidate set is required.

decisions.title: An explicit componentwise terminal objective is still not a plant certificate
decisions.detail: R191 compares withhold, bounded retained effort, and the separately WBC-admitted support-free command at a declared ballistic root-impact plane. Vertical specific energy is candidate-independent; terminal tilt/rate, joint headroom/speed, effort, and admission remain separate, and a candidate must improve one without regressing any. All mechanism gates pass in three complete runs of 481 queries with exact independent re-audit; online selector/re-audit maxima span 0.992–8.106/0.972–1.102 µs. Both sagittal green rows survive and handle/5 ms improves +1.340 s, but left/right boundaries regress up to −0.680 s. The candidate consequence model needs calibrated realization error or richer actions before promotion.

decisions.title: A fresh support-free WBC brake is valid authority machinery, not the right universal objective
decisions.detail: R190 authors ballistic gravity plus attitude/joint damping from current state, solves a separate zero-contact floating WBC, and emits only typed FreshSupportFreeInexactObservation selection 5. Across 247 selections it is admitted below 1e-8 violation, carries zero support/contact-force witness, never refreshes primary age, and replays exactly. Plant consequence rejects universal execution: left falls move +0.450/+0.885 s later, but forward/backward 5 ms green rows newly fall and right/handle/low-friction rows regress, worst −1.935 s. An explicit terminal-impact objective and conservative multi-candidate chooser are required.

decisions.title: A causal forecast-improvement margin is not a monotone plant-safety ordering
decisions.detail: R189 requires the support-free Q15 argmin to beat zero authority by a finite nonnegative margin before Rust spends retained effort. All mechanism gates pass across 127,865 first-run ticks and exact replay. No tested margin from zero through fully withheld passes both 5/10 ms consequence slices. Margin 0.001 removes r188's new green fall but advances one 5 ms and three 10 ms boundaries; the withheld endpoint advances five. More withholding can make a boundary earlier, so scalar score erosion is rejected as authority. The next comparison needs a separately admitted contact-independent brake or explicit terminal-impact objective.

decisions.title: Current-state reduced-score argmin is not plant authority
decisions.detail: R188 removes future burst knowledge and makes selection allocation-free and Rust-owned. On every unavailable tick, support is forced unknown and 0/0.25/0.5/0.75/1 retained-effort fractions are scored from current reduced root state plus the previous achieved-acceleration/resource witness; ties choose less authority. All causal, dormant, replay, exact-effort, finite, and allocation gates pass. Strict consequence rejects the argmin: full authority is selected 159/247 times, backward-4 N/5 ms becomes a new 3.000 s fall, and six prior boundaries advance, worst −1.995 s. A conservative improvement/uncertainty gate or explicit terminal-impact objective is required.

decisions.title: A gain that fits a known future outage duration is not causal authority
decisions.detail: R187 adds Q15 gains 0.45 and 0.95 and scores 5 ms and 10 ms fault classes separately. Both pass the known 10 ms slice, while no gain passes 5 ms and none passes both. On the first unavailable tick those classes have identical evidence, so selecting the duration-specific gain would consume future information. Exact dormancy, withheld-zero semantics, Q15 effort equality, replay, finiteness, allocation, and GC all pass. Non-monotone neighboring outcomes also reject interpolation as a certificate.

decisions.title: Continuous retained-effort authority is valid machinery, not one global dropout policy
decisions.detail: R186 adds a Rust Q15 authority fraction to the typed one-tick inexact-observation hold. Scaling is exact and non-compounding; zero disables retained authority and exactly matches the withheld control. The same first-loss fraction is used before knowing whether loss lasts 5 or 10 ms. All mechanism gates pass, but none of 0/0.25/0.5/0.75/1 passes strict consequence. Each advances an existing fall boundary or creates a new fall; 0.5 changes forward_4n_reference/drop5 from recovered to a 2.495 s fall. A future selector must be state/forecast-conditioned or optimize an explicit terminal objective.

decisions.title: A typed unavailable-evidence hold is valid machinery, not a universal fixed-duration policy
decisions.detail: R185 adds a distinct Rust selection/provenance/status for bounded replay of the last admitted effective effort. Startup, exact transitions, expiry, and reordered ticks cannot use it; held ticks emit no contact-force witness and do not refresh primary health. Exact hold-0/1/2 streams are identical and all 274 selected holds replay the preceding effort exactly with zero allocation/GC. Policy promotion is rejected: one tick leaves three earlier boundaries including handle/10 ms at −1.655 s, while two ticks regresses left, handle, and low friction. The mechanism remains available for a separately proved state-conditioned selector.

decisions.title: Unavailable observation cannot default to zero torque as a safe consequence
decisions.detail: R184 defers periodic dropout until primary authority is established and compares it with the same tick-zero-starting pattern. Every unavailable tick correctly withholds and emits zero torque, all exact-green rows survive, replay is exact, and allocation/GC stay zero. Physical consequence still rejects the behavior: ten case/profile boundaries move earlier. Established 5 ms gaps advance left, right, and handle falls by 0.685/0.350/1.245 s; established 10 ms gaps advance mirrored and low-friction falls by 0.155/0.015 s. Fail-closed provenance is therefore necessary but insufficient; unavailable evidence needs its own separately admitted bounded command.

decisions.title: Steady observation age and latency onset are different authority faults
decisions.detail: R183 shows that r182's 20 ms profile changed from zero-age prestart evidence to older runtime acquisition, causing four backwards-timestamp rejections and four or five fail-closed startup ticks. The corrected steady stream advances the receiver clock and primes three already-aged samples before actuator enable. Across seven paired-replay cases it is 20 ms old from the first runtime tick, has zero timestamp faults and zero withheld ticks, and preserves every plant, command, and terminal bit against exact observation. This is specific to fixed-effective-effort realization and does not make delayed contact universally safe. Five periodic-dropout boundary regressions and synchronous timing remain rejected.

decisions.title: Current-support admission may prove an effective torque, but may not silently replace or refresh it
decisions.detail: R181 runs a raw independently optimized current-support transfer as a causal negative control: it changes terminal boundary or qualification in 16/20 rows. The admitted arm fixes the already-effective r137 effort, proves achieved acceleration and hard feasibility against the current mask, and gives the typed witness to Rust ContactProgramAuthority. Across 18,209 ticks the selected torque is bit-exact, with 16,982 primary and 1,227 current-support selections, zero withheld/lease/fallback ticks, 2.77e-9 maximum hard violation, exact plant/replay, and zero allocation/GC. Supervisor confidence still follows the raw primary solve; realization cannot manufacture primary freshness. Semantic composition passes, while ordinary-process timing, robustness, and hardware remain rejected.

decisions.title: A one-evaluation flight guard closes action non-regression, not controller authority
decisions.detail: R179 evaluates only the first exact mask-0 candidate after double-support arming. Typed WBC admission is necessary but insufficient: the Rust eight-knot score must improve over inertial continuation by at least 0.10 and achieved root angular acceleration must remain within 40 rad/s². The lease is consumed on either verdict. Seventeen queries yield 11 transfers and six rejections; all ten r137 green rows survive, three red boundaries move later, none move earlier, shadow and selected replay are exact, and timed allocation/GC remain zero. This promotes the conditioned action only inside r177's preserved-primary scaffold. R178 current-observation authority is deliberately disabled, so plant-controller promotion remains rejected.

decisions.title: Contact-program enable is a Rust-owned combiner over admitted commands
decisions.detail: R178 adds generic fixed-capacity ContactProgramAuthority state rather than teaching the WBC or contact filter to invent command lifetime. Fresh primary or current-support commands enter only under exact, mutually consistent raw/stable/hard masks. During activation or deactivation, a separately admitted current-hard-support command may enter only after prior authority when explicitly configured; otherwise only a bounded prior lease may execute. Startup without prior authority withholds. Evidence, mask, command, expiry, and sequence faults are non-executable. R180/r181 now admit its zero-hold fixed-effort plant composition semantically; scheduling, robustness, non-identical action substitution, and hardware remain open.

decisions.title: Unconfirmed contact activation is an enable-state problem, not flight
decisions.detail: R177 keeps the exact r139 observation stream but prevents its startup/reacquisition no-contact hard mask from changing the established primary solve. The non-executing shadow then matches r137 plant state, torque, status, fall-safe state, contact count, and terminal consequence bit-for-bit in all 20 cases, and all 10 retained green rows return. This diagnoses r176's largest regression. The preservation switch is not promotable because its primary support lacks current observation authority. A real transition must explicitly withhold authority, use a bounded retained-command lease, or execute a separately current-support-admitted command.

decisions.title: A typed causal selector does not make the selected action safe
decisions.detail: R176 keeps four authorities distinct: r137 sentinel, measured-contact control, a non-executing r175 shadow, and causal execution, then repeats execution in a fresh run. Exact double support arms; a later exact support loss may request only a separately admitted Solved/SolvedWithSlack row below 1e-8 hard violation. The shadow is physically exact and all 1,703 selections and replay pass this contract without timeout extension, blending, reset, cache resurrection, or rejected-row execution. Promotion is rejected because nine of ten retained green cases physically fall, all ten lose qualification with timing, the measured-contact green row is lost, eight existing fall boundaries move earlier, and 33 five-millisecond overruns occur. The selector remains Python evaluation orchestration until revised semantics pass the complete plant gate.

decisions.title: Observed support selects a request, but only a separate WBC may authorize it
decisions.detail: R175 separates three facts that r136 blended: the exact current support observation, the low-energy contingency request, and current dynamics/contact/effort admission. Double support targets the wheel midpoint, left/right support target the sole observed wheel, and flight emits exact ballistic gravity. The request generator is allocation-free and order-independent; all 256 retained actions pass a fresh typed WBC query with exact replay. This admits an instantaneous mechanism only. It does not extend a cached command, reset the plant, or claim recovery through changing contact.

decisions.title: Independent planner/final workspaces may exchange an immutable exact feasibility witness
decisions.detail: R174 keeps both arms on the established every-tick 512-sweep planner profile and uncapped final authority. Rust copies a complete key, primal point, logical diagnostics, and—only for an unfinished Dykstra prefix—the row multipliers. The destination rebuilds its own ordered hard problem and bit-compares every dimension, stable ID, coefficient, bound, tolerance, active-set budget, equality-repair mode, and sparse arithmetic flag. Only projection ceiling/continuation slots may differ, only bounded-to-uncapped. Exact terminals still run every destination-owned soft level; exhausted prefixes continue from the next sweep and remain fail-closed if the uncapped budget exhausts. Across 20 cases all 11,185 copies are consumed, including 54 resumptions; authority, execution, replay, and 18,332,262 logical projections are exact; misses fall 5→0 with no Rust allocation or Python GC. This admits the host-native evaluation compute profile, not the viability action or controller.

decisions.title: Uniform cross-tick planner decimation clears timing but starves confirmation
decisions.detail: R171 makes cadence an explicit tick-sequence contract: period-three updates, typed no-update holds, a matching request-age bound, and a matching confirmation gap. The full matrix is deterministic, replay-exact, finite, allocation-free, and has zero 5 ms misses. It is not semantically or physically acceptable: planner queries fall 20,854→6,904, but all 26 executable request ticks disappear and two retained boundaries move earlier. The next scheduler must preserve the per-tick proposal/confirmation stream through pipelining or a background worker with fresh state/support revalidation; uniform polling reduction is rejected.

decisions.title: Hard-feasibility reuse is session-local, bit-identical, and logically audited
decisions.detail: R169 permits reuse only after exact vector equality on a fixed-capacity key containing DOF, ordered stable IDs, every hard coefficient and lower/upper bound as IEEE-754 bits, and every feasibility-profile parameter. Exact or polished seeds restore the hard solution and then independently solve the current soft hierarchy. Exhausted results restore the same terminal violation and return typed MaxIterations without command authority. Logical sweep/projection counters retain the cold values, an explicit reuse bit exposes physical elision, and planner/final-authority FloatingWbcSession instances share no workspace. The 20-case cold/reuse/replay matrix is exact and allocation-free, but two synchronous misses reject promotion.

decisions.title: A causal bounded viability request is admitted as a mechanism, not as a recovery controller
decisions.detail: R148 makes execution generic and fail-closed; r149 rejects the 40-query action; r150 separates support-program admission; r151–r154 bound the multi-step scorer and causal plant gate. R155 bounds polling; r156 requires two aligned same-support improvements; r157 localizes hybrid-support error. R158 separates shadow from execution, passes all 19 mechanisms, eliminates earlier fall boundaries, preserves the useful left-2 N correction, and suppresses diagonal/up regressions; 58 deadline overruns still reject promotion. R159 rejects a global calibrated maximum on independent holdout: 98.231% overall, 95.681% at 240 ms, and a 14.275× worst miss. Physical promotion remains rejected; the next action needs deterministic timing and conditioned reachable bounds with fresh holdout, not a scalar wake, lifetime tweak, or empirical percentile presented as certainty.

decisions.title: Local viability descent is a bounded search problem, not another static gain
decisions.detail: R146's 245-query oracle finds local 250 ms forecast descent in 15/16 frozen states across double, single, and zero support, so the Upkie boundary is not simply devoid of state-local authority. Only 9/16 oracle forecasts finish inside the declared unit boundary and 15/16 choose a request edge, rejecting direct gain promotion. R147's two-pass yaw→roll→lateral search gives strict descent in all 12 activated rows with 40 exact queries, 1.011 median pressure ratio to the oracle, 3.808 ms p99 summed Rust work, exact replay, and zero allocation. R148 supplies the previously missing execution supervisor, while r149 proves the smoothed action still fails deadline and physical non-regression. The offline result remains valuable as a local authority query, not a deployable recovery objective.

decisions.title: Contact evidence, hard-row eligibility, stable mode, and executable action are four separate admissions
decisions.detail: R139 exact absence removes hard eligibility immediately, while debounced support mode changes only after consecutive evidence; held or rejected samples never author hard rows. R140 proves that an equation-feasible reduced-support WBC result is not automatically executable. R141 proves that withholding it and expiring the prior command is also not a recovery action. R142 proves that the current WBC's equalized normal-load share does not predict the binary edge. R143 supplies a separately typed bounded command lease; r144 rejects strict lease-only plant execution; and r145 rejects composing bounded contact grace ahead of r137's continuous fade. Live promotion therefore requires an independently solved support-state/viability program, not a boolean mask, timeout, or cached command wired into execution.

decisions.title: Contact activity is an observation, not a permanent property of a WBC target
decisions.detail: R138 resolves exact wheel-subtree-to-world contact identity in the replaceable plant and replays frozen states through the same persistent Rust WBC with only the active mask changed. Total MuJoCo contact count is insufficient because it does not name support. A stale hard RollingWheel row may produce MaxIterations with a large hard violation; that diagnostic candidate remains non-executable. Measured contact makes the frozen local equations feasible but does not authorize an action. Live promotion requires causal/debounced observations plus separately admitted double→single→zero-contact transition semantics.

decisions.title: Command freshness may be promoted independently of a recovery controller
decisions.detail: R137 promotes only a Rust-owned lease on the last admitted command. A current MaxIterations candidate never executes; the prior admitted torque is unchanged for five rejection ticks and fades to zero by tick twelve. Admitted primary objectives are not blended, so nominal and 4 N recovery remain bit-exact. Promotion additionally requires no earlier frozen adverse boundary, reduced stale age in every adverse row, exact replay, finite traces, and zero timed Rust allocation. The r136 tilt/rate/height damping blend remains rejected and is not hidden inside this freshness contract.

decisions.title: A contingency mechanism and its deployment are separate admissions
decisions.detail: R136 makes failure handling explicit: four continuous evidence channels select a bounded Primary→Degraded→Contingency transition, a damping candidate is solved through the ordinary WBC, stale command authority expires, and Fallen remains latched until reset. Evaluation admission requires deterministic state evolution, bounded slew, finite first-boundary traces, exact replay, zero timed Rust allocation, preserved nominal semantics, and retained 4 N recovery. Deployment additionally requires physical non-regression. The mechanism passes while deployment fails because the 6 N overload falls 3.120 s earlier; neither a clean state machine nor reduced authority can be called safer without that plant gate.

decisions.title: Local task authority is a response curve, not a recovery certificate
decisions.detail: R135 evaluates both request signs at 1/10/50/250 native acceleration units for six root axes and four explicit contact modes. Rust returns achieved generalized acceleration, per-layer RMS/clipping, hard residual, friction and effort margins, status, work, and allocations. Python may summarize the signed directional response but may not collapse those witnesses into one health value. A feasible local acceleration does not prove a policy can enter, remain in, or return to the viability set; r133 remains the external-plant consequence gate and r134 remains a rejected controller candidate.

decisions.title: A contact basis is runtime physical data, and an A/B may pass while promotion fails
decisions.detail: The floating WBC already consumes tangent-X, tangent-Y, and normal in world coordinates. R134 exposes those orthonormal bases through the fixed-shape Python boundary per tick and target; all bases are validated atomically before any output changes. The planar Upkie candidate rotates that basis with measured heading and keeps steering state in Rust. Its evaluator passes completeness, baseline reproduction, exact replay, allocation, numeric integrity, and discrimination, while promotion separately requires preserved nominal/sagittal behavior plus actual recovery of every declared lateral row. Delaying a fall, retaining a positive DCM support-segment margin, or recovering one sign at a lucky gain cannot authorize the controller.

decisions.title: Evaluation admission and controller recovery are separate verdicts
decisions.detail: The 20-case r133 matrix admits its instrumentation only when the frozen case set is complete, all three force axes and repeated impulses are present, traces are finite, canonical recovery repeats exactly, green and red rows coexist, the paired lateral fall boundary and friction boundary discriminate, every failure stops on its first threshold, no pre-boundary numeric fault occurs, and Rust timed regions allocate zero bytes. Individual rows independently report RECOVERED, FALL, UNSETTLED, or NUMERIC_FAULT plus qualification blockers. A red controller row is useful boundary evidence and cannot fail the evaluator merely for being red; post-fall integration is forbidden from polluting latency or inventing a later numeric classification.

decisions.title: Rolling kinematics and contact virtual work share one Jacobian
decisions.detail: For RollingWheel, the longitudinal no-slip row is J_center,x qdd + c qdd_wheel plus bias/stabilization. The same J_center,x + c·e_wheel maps tangent contact force into generalized dynamics. The Rust regression checks both coefficients together, and the independent 64-state Pinocchio replay reconstructs augmented dynamics to 1.87e-11 L∞ with zero timed allocation. R130 adds rooted capture/station composition and a separate soft-contact plant consequence without weakening this state-local admission boundary.

decisions.title: Python owns the replaceable plant; Rust owns reference/controller state
decisions.detail: MuJoCo parses the pinned Upkie only after an explicit floating root is inserted, keeps static-body fusion disabled, and adds only ground plus URDF-limited torque motors—no invented damping or armature. Every observation crosses PyO3 into persistent Rust capture/WBC sessions and every admitted torque returns to MuJoCo. Rejected candidates never execute: the adapter holds the last admitted command while preserving diagnostic status. R131 exposes this exact boundary through a supervised per-session worker; Python never decides force validity, request lifetime, command expiry, or browser protocol semantics.

decisions.title: A PUSH point is bounded wrench authority, not display metadata
decisions.detail: The browser authors body, world force, and world application point. Rust grants the command only when the body exists in the latest plant snapshot and the point is within 750 mm of its streamed origin; force remains independently capped at 8 N and expires after 140 ms without refresh. Python owns the MuJoCo topology needed to check the exact COM lever, then calls mj_applyFT. The streamed moment is τ=(p−x_COM)×F and remains separate from force. R132 independently predicts and observes the ±200 mm moment differential and signed pitch consequence; an invalid lever clears only the active push and cannot terminate the session.

decisions.title: The torso handle is a Cartesian base target, not a squat mode
decisions.detail: TORSO · BASE uses the same green target/ghost semantics as other handles. In TARGET, its XYZ displacement maps to the floating base and planar leg IK keeps the two wheel anchors explicit; there is no hidden lowering/raising clamp or squat button. In PUSH, the same visible body point authors a bounded wrench application on the measured MuJoCo body. Green target intent and orange physical disturbance use distinct command types, sockets, snapshots, and authority labels.

decisions.title: Unreachable interactive intent is soft; trajectory validity is not
decisions.detail: R126 keeps infeasible Cartesian or angular intent outside the feasible set and exposes its residual. Cartesian frame drag and typed joint drag remain distinct because a point endpoint cannot select the knee branch through a straight-leg singularity. The Rust controller uniformly backtracks the solved velocity for at most twelve fixed steps and rebuilds the complete quintic on each step; it accepts only exact position, velocity, acceleration, jerk, and configured collision validity. Joint-velocity bounds reserve a later braking horizon. If neither primary nor braking trajectory is valid, the command-side adapter emits a stationary represented-state hold and retries normally on the next tick. This hold is fail-closed command evidence, not a physically realizable instantaneous stop or plant guarantee. Release is idempotent and clears point, joint, and squat engagement. Per-coordinate position/stopping arrays remain available when multiple joints are simultaneously critical; the global limiting coordinate is only a view, never the sole evidence. A read-only FK query computes test and UI frame locations without mutating controller state.

decisions.title: Resource availability is explicit state, not inferred health
decisions.detail: R125 accepts externally authored acceleration and actuator-effort scales in [0,1] and applies them directly to nominal configured bounds for exactly one state-local query. Bounds and utilization telemetry share the same values; nominal bounds are restored between calls. A scale may come from a calibrated thermal, electrical, reliability, or safety adapter, but the WBC does not invent that cause. Tracking residual, hard-equation residual, solver status, bound contact, and physical plant realization remain separate evidence.

decisions.title: Contact schedules are explicit data at the state-local boundary
decisions.detail: R124 accepts one immutable mode and activity value per query/target but carries no hidden contact state. LockedPoint owns XYZ, NormalPoint owns Z, RollingPoint owns YZ, and RollingWheel owns wheel-coupled X plus YZ. Schema faults reject the entire call before outputs change; valid physical infeasibility remains a solver status. This admits composition and deterministic mode changes without pretending to provide contact estimation, impacts, or hybrid stability. A future estimator or simulator must be separately versioned and measured against this exact CPU reference.

decisions.title: State-local rolling admission is the CPU semantic gate
decisions.detail: The canonical Upkie composition test has no balance policy, state integrator, simulator, or carried contact state. Python supplies immutable root/joint states and explicit RollingWheel descriptors; Rust emits and solves one floating [qdd, actuator torque, contact force] hierarchy. Pinocchio rebuilds M, h, J, and J-dot-v, while friction, unilateral force, URDF effort, task residuals, qdd saturation, work budget, allocations, and status remain separate witnesses. SolvedWithSlack proves hard physical admission, never exact realization of every lower objective. CUDA batching may optimize only after reproducing this CPU boundary.

decisions.title: Rust guts, Python eval land
decisions.detail: Control-path topology, math, state, and allocation ownership stay in Rust. Python operates through fixed-shape batch arrays.

decisions.title: Upkie is the interactive reference; browser cadence is not controller cadence
decisions.detail: The hosted editor loads the pinned Upkie URDF and authored meshes. TARGET controller states and physical PUSH states use separate typed WebSockets at 50 Hz; the browser interpolates only the active source, refreshes telemetry at 10 Hz, and bounds held-wrench refresh to 20 Hz. Perspective/orbit/pan/view-plane mapping remain presentation adapters. TARGET preserves authored Cartesian intent through WBC rejection; PUSH renders only measured MuJoCo transforms and independent capture/station/actuator/CPU authority. Lost transport ghosts the last state and disables the affected controls. The toy humanoid remains an explicit evaluation fixture.

decisions.title: Interactive services have named replace-in-place ownership
decisions.detail: The current CLI deployment runs one bonesaw-public server on port 8777 and one bonesaw-tunnel Quick Tunnel; the legacy bonesaw-local name is stopped during every replacement and stays inactive. Start first stops and verifies those exact project names, removes only absolute-path Bonesaw/known-port Quick-Tunnel orphans, refuses an unrelated 8777 listener, scopes URL discovery to the current systemd invocation, and verifies Upkie through public HTTP plus WebSocket before publishing. It never touches the machine's unrelated named Cloudflare tunnel.

decisions.title: Motion-corpus semantics remain in Python
decisions.detail: Python verifies and reconstructs pinned CMU ASF/AMC bytes, separates periodic body motion from absolute stride, converts endpoint motion into contact-consistent anchored foot paths, classifies support by bilateral filtered endpoint height with a 5 mm overlap, applies rooted forward/lateral scaling and startup phase ramp, and scores fixed-shape outputs. Rust owns measured touchdown anchors, target shaping, velocity viability, contact fallback, every solve/integration step, and all timed ticks.

decisions.title: CPU exact before CUDA batch
decisions.detail: CpuExactF64 remains the StrictLexicographic semantic reference. R97 freezes the separate FixedLevelApproximate CpuMirrorF32 hierarchy before device solve work. CudaMirrorF32 must reproduce its fingerprinted algorithm and pass independent D1/D3 and isolation gates; CudaThroughputF32 remains a separately fingerprinted relaxed profile and cannot inherit mirror certification.

decisions.title: Budget progress, infeasibility, and command admission are separate
decisions.detail: A fixed 64-hard-sweep plus 32-sweeps-per-active-level budget never early-exits. Initial, best, and final hard residuals expose continuous progress. MaxIterations means the budget ended without admission; it does not prove PrimalInfeasible. The best finite candidate is retained for diagnostics while the executable command stays exactly zero.

decisions.title: Dynamic command synthesis is not a plant rollout
decisions.detail: R99 consumes caller-authored observed state for every floating WBC query and separately carries exact commanded actuator position, velocity, and acceleration for trajectory splicing. R100 maps segment coefficients back through the transmission and requires analytic joint-position validity as well as actuator derivative validity. R101 independently sweeps primary and braking geometry on the deterministic servo grid. R102 can additionally require a conservative clearance proof between those samples. It never feeds emitted qdd or samples back into the observation. Solved/SolvedWithSlack plus derivative, position, and configured collision validity may select primary; otherwise an independently valid braking contingency is selected with zero admitted feed-forward effort. Command divergence is retained as evidence, not called tracking.

decisions.title: One physical WBC solve may feed multiple typed read-only witnesses
decisions.detail: R103 exposes advance_solved_into: a caller-supplied solved floating-WBC output is copied into same-layout caller-owned storage, then passes through the exact command-admission transaction. The live adapter no longer repeats the dense physical solve merely to ask trajectory questions. Raw-WBC query time, command-admission time, and four-query frame work remain separate clocks; reusing evidence never turns the guided browser pose into plant realization.

decisions.title: Collision representations and fallbacks are explicit
decisions.detail: R104 compiled one tight primitive per supported authored shape alongside deterministic sphere covers. R107 makes the tight primitive table canonical for both fixed-root differential avoidance and command admission; sphere-cover emission survives only through separately named fallback methods. Cylinders become enclosing capsules; spheres and authored capsules retain their natural representation; oriented boxes use point/segment witnesses and a conservative separating-axis lower bound. Collisionless revolute/fixed carrier chains collapse into physical adjacency, while prismatic carriers remain collision-tested. Representation, quality, exclusions, and pair provenance are never hidden in a health verdict.

decisions.title: Continuous clearance witnesses are pair-consistent
decisions.detail: R105 never subtracts one pair's worst-case speed from another pair's sampled minimum. The dense grid stores a minimum for every stable primitive pair in fixed caller-owned scratch; each lower bound uses that pair's precompiled coordinate-speed coefficients and the segment's analytic maximum joint velocities over half the sample interval. The lowest pair-specific result becomes the continuous witness and carries its stable pair/body provenance. This is conservative Lipschitz evidence, not exact closest-feature CCD.

decisions.title: Adaptive certification is bounded work beneath sampled collision authority
decisions.detail: R106 declares maximum subdivision depth at controller construction. Pairs certified by the broad R105 bound skip all interval-local work; unresolved leaves use analytic subinterval velocity extrema and deterministic midpoint primitive samples. Leaf count, midpoint pair-query count, unresolved count, and reached depth are semantic diagnostics. Any base or midpoint sample below clearance records stable pair/time and terminates further refinement because sampled collision already withholds the command. Refinement may turn uncertainty into a proof or into stronger sampled failure evidence; it may never erase a violation or extend the compute deadline.

decisions.title: Avoidance and admission share one tight-primitive witness
decisions.detail: R107 computes signed distance, stable pair ID, deterministic normal, surface points, locally selected rigid-body feature points, relative normal velocity, and the avoidance Jacobian in one allocation-free primitive witness. Command sampling consumes the same scalar routine and pair table. Sphere and capsule radii do not introduce spurious angular velocity because Jacobians attach to medial features; box support features retain local rotational derivatives. Box-box remains explicitly ConservativePrimitive. R108 reuses this witness in the floating acceleration solve.

decisions.title: Floating collision avoidance is a local viability barrier, not CCD or plant response
decisions.detail: R108 emits J qdd + bias + 2 ζω hdot + ω² h >= 0 for h = tight distance − hard margin. The bias is the current normal projection of rigid-feature Jdot-v. Closest-feature switching and normal curvature are deliberately excluded and named; R106 sampled/adaptive trajectory admission still owns between-tick clearance. Closest pair, limiting active row, unsupported geometry, solver residual, command selection, and realized plant response remain separately typed evidence.

decisions.title: World geometry is an explicit finite authority field, never assumed free
decisions.detail: R109 samples one immutable dense SDF in its authored rigid grid frame, rotates the analytic trilinear gradient into control_world, and subtracts each deterministic conservative body-probe radius. A query outside the known grid either becomes typed unknown evidence under Reject or uses OccupiedBoundary, where the known-volume boundary becomes an additional signed-distance obstacle and outside values are negative. There is no silent free-space fallback. The local HOCBF includes current rigid-point Jdot-v but excludes the SDF Hessian and voxel-feature switching; R110's separate command gate owns between-tick geometry.

decisions.title: Swept world authority composes joints with an explicit root prediction
decisions.detail: R111 pairs each exact mapped joint quintic with an independently constructed six-DoF root prediction anchored in smooth control_world. Every endpoint, 1 ms knot, and adaptive midpoint evaluates both paths before FK and SDF sampling. The field's measured global Lipschitz bound multiplies analytic joint/root twist extrema; root angular speed is converted through a precompiled conservative probe-reach bound. Primary and brake never share validity. This root segment is a bounded collision prediction, not an actuator coordinate, plant rollout, map-frame correction, or claim that the base will realize the pose.

decisions.title: Forecast error consumes authority continuously and deterministically
decisions.detail: R112 attaches six nonnegative worst-case growth parameters to each root prediction: initial translation radius, translation velocity/acceleration error, initial attitude radius, and angular velocity/acceleration error. At time t, each probe loses field-Lipschitz times translation-radius plus compiled root-angular reach times attitude-radius. The erosion-growth derivative joins the between-sample rate proof. Primary and brake retain independent robust minima. These externally declared radii are deterministic contracts, not covariance, confidence intervals, estimator calibration, timeouts, or a claim that the nominal predictor is physically realized.

decisions.title: World-scene freshness is independent authority
decisions.detail: R113 assigns the compiled world field a scene epoch, source time, validity interval, and derived age. Admission requires the expected epoch, a non-future source, tick inclusion, configured maximum age, and validity through the entire command horizon. EpochMismatch, SourceFromFuture, NotYetValid, ExpiredAtTick, HorizonExpired, TooOld, and InvalidStamp are stable typed outcomes. Any invalid snapshot marks both primary and brake world evidence unknown and rejects. Scene epoch is neither MotionProgram epoch nor map/odom correction; control_world stays smooth while map and odom may be externally re-anchored.

decisions.title: Canonical reconstruction and its error envelope are one WBC boundary
decisions.detail: R119 preallocates every floating-state slot and accepts only program-epoch-compatible, finite, manifold-valid, causal, fresh, sufficiently synchronized observations. Exact, local cubic-Hermite interpolation, and bounded prediction retain provenance and hard eligibility. Their typed error envelope grows from query exposure plus synchronization uncertainty using separate joint q/v, root translation/rotation, represented-point, and CoM rates. Joint stopping intersects all q±error,v±error corners; finite support loses one CoM radius; local self collision loses two represented-point radii; local world collision loses one. R120 freezes local consumption as a continuous bounded-work contract with CPU/jitter, zero-allocation, fixed-size, and replay evidence. R121 passes the same typed object into Primary and brake admission: pair geometry loses two body-local radii, world root forecasts begin with the observation root radius, and SDF probes then lose one local point radius. Raw, root-robust, and fully robust witnesses remain distinct from tracking mismatch. The streamed reconstruction, WBC, command geometry, and selection now share one query timestamp. Held, stale, or invalid output still fails before hard rows. These are deterministic caller-authored bounds, not covariance, calibrated confidence, or plant realization.

decisions.title: Command mismatch consumes authority before geometry can claim realization
decisions.detail: R114 maps observed q/v into actuator coordinates and compares them with the exact prior-command splice. Position and velocity retain independent limiting actuator IDs and signed contingency/reject headrooms. Warning-level divergence withholds feed-forward effort and the primary segment but may select an independently valid braking segment. Hard divergence rejects both because command-space collision and limit evidence no longer adequately represents the observed mechanism. The evidence detects mismatch only; saturation, delay, contact loss, thermal derating, calibration, and mechanical failure remain separate possible causes.

decisions.title: Unknown or disabled command geometry is never measured clear
decisions.detail: Self-collision validation is an explicit trajectory profile. Disabled validation returns an empty report with Infinity rather than a fabricated clearance. Collision-enabled construction counts unsupported authored shapes and rejects them by default; a caller may knowingly select represented-subset validation. Primary and contingency retain independent sampled minima and first-violation pair/time. R105 reports the minimum pair-specific lower bound after subtracting only that pair's relative-speed certificate over half the sample interval. SampledCollision and ContinuousClearance flags cannot be confused.

decisions.title: Batch conformance is an authority stack, not a backend boolean
decisions.detail: Program/layout fingerprint, declared stage manifest, arithmetic profile, repeat determinism, f64-oracle error, agent isolation, allocation behavior, timing distribution, and device availability are independently reported. A missing CUDA executor is UNAVAILABLE, not a CPU-emulated pass, and none of these backend gates replaces physical WBC authority evidence.

decisions.title: CUDA mirror stages are admitted independently and never borrow CPU evidence
decisions.detail: R91–R96 implement StateInput through fixed row emission; R98 adds the seventh HierarchicalSolve module and launch. The Driver API executor owns context, immutable model/query/task/contact/solve constants, and fixed state/product/row/bounds/command/candidate/diagnostic/scratch buffers. Execution has no CPU fallback. Source policy, CPU mirror witness, six NVRTC compilers, runtime presence, and device D1/D3 are separate gates: here source/CPU pass, NVRTC is library_unavailable, runtime is no_device, and device gates are NOT RUN. The solve-stage capability may be true while full cuda_mirror_f32 and Graph stay false. Actuation, integration, and Graph require separate evidence.

decisions.title: Rigid-patch topology comes from geometry; the basis score is not frozen
decisions.detail: R87 optionally derives exactly six independent rigid-body rows from same-frame force-point geometry, rejects collinear or deficient patches, centers coordinates for frame-origin invariance, and fingerprints the chosen modes. Maximum minimum singular value is the current deterministic selection score. It slightly improves geometric σmin, but its solve p50 is +33.5% at one agent and −8.2%/−6.1% at 8/32 versus the handwritten R85 basis, proving that geometric conditioning alone is not a universal solver-work proxy. The physical hard manifold is admitted; the canonical tie-break and score remain open.

decisions.title: The browser pose is a state-local authority query, not a physics rollout
decisions.detail: R88's guided flat-foot adapter applies the commanded squat and planar disturbance pose, then asks the same raw floating WBC for dynamics/contact feasibility, finite-CoP reserve, joint-stopping reserve, effort use, task compromise, and solver work. It does not infer body response from self-integrating acceleration. A sustained unguided self-integration probe reached NumericalFailure and is retained as a failed experiment; hardware or simulated response requires a separately admitted plant and policy.

decisions.title: Per-query and frame-batch compute clocks are separate authority resources
decisions.detail: R90 defines solve_us as the maximum end-to-end state-local query represented by one streamed frame. query_count and query_batch_us separately expose the sum of the four 5 ms queries used by the 50 Hz adapter. The 5 ms limit applies to the maximum query and the 20 ms limit to the batch; transport, JSON serialization, network delay, and browser rendering require a separately named end-to-end clock. A batch sum can never be compared with the single-query limit again.

decisions.title: One smooth control root
decisions.detail: control_world owns the robot root; odom and map are reporting roots so localization jumps cannot kick the WBC.

decisions.title: Five strict priority levels
decisions.detail: Invariant, Viability, Intent, Preference, and Style are lexicographic—not a tunable weighted sum.

decisions.title: Task declarations stay fixed while inert dense rows compact
decisions.detail: The compiled five-layer task declaration and public residual/provenance shape never change. Exact-zero rows may be skipped internally at any level; nonzero rows may be skipped only at terminal Style when every referenced coordinate has a finite equal lower/upper bound and the fixed value exactly meets the target. This is feasible-set work removal, not authority-layer deletion. The explicit resolved-task-row-compaction-control feature preserves the pre-r66 solve for differential checks.

decisions.title: No controller heap traffic
decisions.detail: Tasks, constraints, pseudoinverse matrices, collisions, segments, samples, and diagnostics reuse caller-owned storage.

decisions.title: Actuators are explicit program coordinates
decisions.detail: MotionProgram schema 6 contains stable actuator IDs, actuator-space velocity/acceleration/effort/jerk limits, generalized-from-actuator transmission, and an optional reverse command map. Effort uses the power-consistent transpose map. The URDF fallback is an explicit identity transmission, not a runtime assumption; coupled or passive mechanisms replace it at authoring time and change the program fingerprint.

decisions.title: Coupled effort limits stay coupled inside WBC
decisions.detail: For a square invertible transmission q̇=G ȧ, the dynamic solve retains generalized effort variables but emits one hard stable row per actuator: lower≤G[:,a]ᵀτq≤upper. The Style objective uses the same Gᵀ map, diagnostics report actuator-space headroom and limiting actuator, and no per-joint box approximation is permitted. A non-square passive or overactuated topology remains rejected until MotionProgram carries an explicit generalized-force actuation operator.

decisions.title: Persistent actuator authority is model state, not QP folklore
decisions.detail: A calibrated optional actuator profile advances winding temperature with an exact constant-input lumped thermal step and reports current, copper loss, signed mechanical power, ideal electrical power, continuous physical derating, available effort, headroom, and utilization. UI warning thresholds remain external. No live robot may claim temperature or reliability from instantaneous torque alone; absent calibration is UNMODELED and a declared-but-unconnected profile is UNAVAILABLE.

decisions.title: Admission is a three-stage certificate
decisions.detail: Authored root/CoM/end-effector arrays first pass the standalone centroidal/contact contract, then an allocation-free morphology projection produces joint position and analytic velocity/acceleration jets, then stateless floating WBC admits the projected jet under dynamics, contact, friction, torque, and acceleration constraints. Authored-to-projected tracking error and projected-to-WBC task error remain separate gates; no policy, integration, or simulator may enter this path.

decisions.title: Oracle tasks share one generalized acceleration witness
decisions.detail: A stateless WBC certificate may not command one generalized acceleration while scoring point, angular, or CoM rows against unrelated bias-only targets. R54 derives each task's physical acceleration as Jq̈+J̇q̇ from the same morphology-projected jet, and a material stance contact requests zero physical point acceleration because the WBC subtracts J̇q̇ internally. Root attitude/height are structural Invariants while horizontal root/CoM transfer is Viability, matching the integrated profile. Hard admission and tracking remain separate check groups even when both pass.

decisions.title: Oracle boundaries follow the semantic stage
decisions.detail: PlaCo is the independent fixed-base task/solver behavior reference, Pinocchio is the frame and rigid-body product oracle, and pinned upstream Upkie C++ is the rolling-controller law oracle. R64 composes Pinocchio products with a separate NumPy lexicographic equality solver to test the compact fixed-effort WBC boundary without consuming Bonesaw products or workspace. Parameter-aligned parity and live tuned behavior remain separate claims. Ruckig remains reserved for the optional jerk-limited trajectory mode rather than being misapplied to WBC.

decisions.title: Typed signal IR inside MotionProgram
decisions.detail: A flat topologically ordered scalar/vector/rotation graph carries value, velocity, and acceleration jets. Rotations use unit quaternions with world angular derivatives and stateful SO(3) filters/springs. Stable IDs, inferred types, state-slot layout, named outputs, resolved kinematic tasks, and floating root/CoM response profiles are canonical archive data. Runtime memory is explicit and double-buffered.

decisions.title: Stable-ID authoring, fixed-slot task execution
decisions.detail: Task specs name signal outputs by stable ID; compilation resolves each to a fixed output slot/frame and serializes the TaskOp. Kinematic point/CoM/orientation/direction-aim and floating root-attitude/root-translation/CoM tasks now share this boundary. Floating response profiles also freeze damping, acceleration caps, priorities, and per-block weights.

decisions.title: Emission correctness is not whole-body authority
decisions.detail: R79 point attractors emit critical-damped physical acceleration from target position/velocity/acceleration jets, then subtract Jdot-v; contact locks emit the same fixed three-axis Jacobian with desired material-point acceleration minus Jdot-v. Weight and strict priority remain descriptor metadata for the later hierarchy rather than scaling physical-unit rows. Inactive rows are exact zeros without changing topology. A shared-qdd least-squares residual exposes simultaneous conflict continuously, but row admission does not claim hard feasibility, bounded solver convergence, actuator realization, thermal reliability, or integrated body response.

decisions.title: Direction aim is an S² task, not an orientation task
decisions.detail: DirectionAim consumes a vector jet, normalizes the authored frame axis at compile time, differentiates the desired world direction in its tangent plane, and emits angular tracking velocity through (I − aaᵀ)Jω. Rotation about the controlled axis is absent from both Jacobian and target, so gaze and aim do not silently constrain roll. The operation still occupies a fixed three-row slot; its geometric rank is two.

decisions.title: Fixed task slots are also diagnostic provenance
decisions.detail: Every floating-base tick reports fourteen fixed slots: nine semantic base slots (root angular, root horizontal, root height, joint posture, optional subset-joint acceleration, optional CoM, optional centroidal angular-momentum rate, contact force, actuator torque), one arbitrary-frame angular-acceleration slot, and four Cartesian point-acceleration slots. Each records activity, rows, priority, physical-unit L2/RMS residual, and clipping in caller-owned storage.

decisions.title: Authority is continuous, typed, and deadline-bounded
decisions.detail: Requested pose, instantaneous feasibility, causal effort realization, state-local acceleration consequence, persistent physical authority, and numerical convergence are different signals. The core produces threshold-free typed residual, signed margin, headroom, utilization, clipping, bounded-work, electrical-power, temperature, and continuous derating evidence. R63 keeps acceleration, unilateral force, friction, and support pressure separate even when one fixed-effort equality query produces them together. Absolute warning/critical contracts live in a versioned adapter or evaluator profile and corpus percentiles remain observations beside them. The browser transports its profile and resource-model availability in Hello; it does not hide alert constants or invent one aggregate health score. Persistent derating constrains future solves but never rewrites the historical instantaneous evidence.

decisions.title: Unified dynamic decision vector
decisions.detail: The CPU profiles solve one strict problem over [root q̈, joint q̈, τ, contact force], omitting root torque. Contact acceleration and every rigid-body equation are hard rows. Root, posture, subset-joint acceleration, CoM, centroidal angular-momentum rate, one arbitrary-frame angular acceleration, and up to four arbitrary frame-point acceleration tasks are separate lexicographic operations with stable provenance.

decisions.title: Centroidal angular momentum is an external-wrench task
decisions.detail: The floating centroidal map measures current angular momentum about the system CoM. A preallocated three-row task maps each contact-force basis through (contact point − CoM) × force and requests angular-momentum rate directly; gravity contributes zero moment about the CoM. Python may supply zero-momentum damping frequency, weight, and strict priority, but the Rust solver owns every task row and timed tick. Unit coverage reconstructs the achieved external moment from solved contact forces.

decisions.title: Support centre is not a CoM reference
decisions.detail: The support centroid belongs to a balance law as a ZMP/CoP target or bound, not as a directly tracked CoM trajectory. Revision r33 derives measured DCM from CoM position/velocity, builds and erodes the established support hull in fixed Rust storage, clips virtual ZMP, and emits a horizontal LIPM acceleration without Python callbacks or tick allocations. The first-swing improvement is real, but full-transfer failure keeps the reference planner and task coupling provisional rather than canonical.

decisions.title: Evaluation references declare bounded future influence
decisions.detail: Python owns pinned-corpus interpretation, but every preview parameter must describe its true causal horizon. The DCM oracle now performs a fixed receding-horizon backward recurrence, while floating lateral registration uses the canonical CMU cycle rather than runtime output length. Extension-invariant root/endpoint/contact/cadence/phase tests and a beyond-horizon perturbation test prevent end-of-buffer tuning from masquerading as controller improvement.

decisions.title: Reference feasibility precedes WBC tracking
decisions.detail: A generator must first pass an open-loop contract using only authored root, CoM, foot jets, contact schedule, and sole geometry. Effective/retimed targets, tracked state, policy, solve status, forces, residuals, latency, and physics are forbidden inputs.
