Positive normal force, friction demand, conditional zero-angular-momentum CoP, reach, and contact continuity are scored before any controller comparison. R42 is the first admitted G1 trace: a Rust two-stage LIPM boundary plan passes 9/9 gates while PlaCo remains an independent 8/9 oracle.

decisions.title: One measured phase cursor retimes the complete reference
decisions.detail: Rust owns persistent source phase and applied-rate state. A pure touchdown policy derives the fastest safe rate from measured sole error, whole-patch tangential speed, normal speed, acceleration capacity, and the unchanged contact-admission envelope. One cursor samples quintic root, CoM, every endpoint jet, and discrete contact intent; velocity and acceleration use the full time-warp chain rule. The evaluator requires the first post-liftoff authored touchdown to be reached, so holding before an unsafe edge cannot score as a vacuous success.

decisions.title: Capture-margin cadence is diagnostic, not production policy
decisions.detail: A pure allocation-free Rust law maps signed DCM support margin through a C1 taper and min-combines it with touchdown phase rate. Immediate engagement injects 56.1 s⁻¹ phase acceleration and is rejected; bounded engagement improves tracking and the clean prefix, but neither 600 nor 800 ticks produces an admissible landing. The switch remains disabled by default. Phase policy cannot make an inconsistent pelvis/CoM/contact reference dynamically feasible.

decisions.title: Contact failure is typed, never hidden
decisions.detail: Rust owns explicit Swing, Precontact, TouchdownNormal, Locked, and NormalFallback states per target. A planned landing latches a sole-center position and foot rotation, uses bounded cubic translation and angular PD tasks before contact, then admits a full sole lock only after minimum dwell and whole-patch tangential speed viability. Failed rigid lock and released contact remain separate solver statuses and raw telemetry.

decisions.title: Joint-limit integration preserves tangent consistency
decisions.detail: When floating integration reaches a finite URDF joint limit, outward velocity is projected to zero while inward velocity remains admissible. Configuration can no longer clamp at a limit while the next Jacobian and bias pass observe impossible motion. Upper, lower, and inward-release cases are regression tested.

decisions.title: Velocity viability is smooth and explicit
decisions.detail: The CPU core maps authored joint-speed utilization through a cubic smoothstep that is exactly zero below its activation threshold and requests bounded inward acceleration at the effective controller limit. The Rust Python boundary builds only active coordinates in preallocated vectors. It shares the fixed subset-joint task slot with protected posture and simultaneous use is rejected. r34 proves useful capture authority but rejects always-on promotion, so the feature remains an opt-in ablation.

decisions.title: Measured phase schedules authority continuously
decisions.detail: The CPU core classifies measured support as Unsupported, SingleSupport, Precontact, or MultiSupport and selects validated nonnegative soft-task scales. Engagement may be immediate while release is bounded per tick without overshoot. The Rust batch path owns persistent scalar state and streams phase, applied scale, and active coordinate count. r35 rejects phase-only promotion but preserves this deterministic mechanism for feedback scheduling.

decisions.title: Capture margin closes the authority loop
decisions.detail: The DCM controller reports minimum signed inward distance to the same eroded convex support polygon used for virtual-ZMP clipping. A cubic-smooth Rust law combines capture margin, root-attitude error, and precontact age into target authority; bounded release produces the applied scale. r36 improves timing but observes margins below -85 cm, proving that authority alone cannot repair the fixed landing/reference.

decisions.title: Capture landing is bounded, reachable, and committed
decisions.detail: A pure Rust policy moves the latched sole-center anchor only along the authored-to-DCM ray. An analytic ray/sphere intersection enforces the authored horizontal offset and future-root leg-reach limits together; landing height stays authored and anchor speed is bounded per tick. A phase horizon freezes the target before contact, after which measured proximity and patch velocity retime admission. r37 improves the clean prefix to tick 482, but 172 post-edge observations remain too far and too fast, so complete root/CoM/swing jet retiming remains provisional.

decisions.title: Reference morphology is robot-authored, not invented
decisions.detail: Upkie remains the rolling-controller and dynamics reference. The walking corpus now fetches Unitree's official G1 23-DOF mode-10 URDF at commit f3772ce, verifies SHA-256 9333e89c…, retains the BSD-3-Clause license, and uses Unitree's authored bent-knee nominal posture. Its six-DOF legs replace the structurally underactuated toy-leg walk experiment.

decisions.title: Flat feet are finite support patches
decisions.detail: Python supplies immutable URDF-authored sole geometry; Rust expands each active foot into four caller-capacity force points. The G1 patch uses x=-0.050/0.120 m, y≈±0.0275 m, z=-0.035 m in the ankle-roll frame. Four friction-limited force blocks retain the finite wrench cone, while a rank-minimal Locked + Normal + Rolling row basis emits exactly six independent rigid-foot equations instead of twelve redundant point locks. Rust derives convex-hull edge inequalities over normal forces, erodes the polygon by the declared margin, and now rebuilds those rows for every established contact in both the stateless oracle and ordinary floating session.

decisions.title: Schedules request contact; measured sole state establishes it
decisions.detail: A planned touchdown enters physical contact only when the stored sole material point is within 0.025 m of its landing anchor, whole-patch tangential speed is at most 0.20 m/s, and normal speed is at most 0.20 m/s. If the phase source requests release before an incoming support locks, the established support is retained. Delayed landings continue the bounded cubic landing task without contact forces. The thresholds are validated core configuration; Python only builds the corpus and scores authored-versus-effective support.

decisions.title: Force regularization cannot drive posture
decisions.detail: Joint posture is Preference. Nominal contact-force distribution and actuator-torque regularization are Style, so they may choose among posture-equivalent solutions but cannot accelerate joints merely to equalize corner loads. A static multi-point regression freezes this ordering.

decisions.title: Near-feasible seeds receive exact active-set polish
decisions.detail: The dense half-space feasibility pass hands near-boundary seeds to a preallocated active-set polish. Hard-equality projection remains immutable across every semantic correction, and a tick is accepted only when the original bounds, dynamics, and contact rows all satisfy the 1e-8 contract. Support patches now avoid manufacturing redundant equality rows before this kernel.

decisions.title: Bounded hybrid projection owns the cold hard-feasibility seed
decisions.detail: Every constrained solve begins with at most eight canonical-order Dykstra sweeps. If the original polytope is still outside the near-feasible band, a no-allocation primal/dual active set projects from that immutable working origin, removes negative-dual inequalities, adds the most normalized violated row, and rechecks every original bound and row at 1e-8. Active-set work is capped at 64 iterations and repeated active sets are detected in fixed stack storage. A cycle or exhausted active-set budget is an accelerator miss, not a proof of infeasibility: r30 restores the exact Dykstra state and spends the remainder of the original bounded projection budget before issuing a typed verdict.

decisions.title: Projected inverses are reused only under an exact validity invariant
decisions.detail: Within a priority level, the final projected matrix and pseudoinverse are reused for nullspace freezing only when no rank-one bound/inequality update changed the nullspace after that decomposition. Otherwise the dense kernel is recomputed. Per-tick and per-priority pseudoinverse, Jacobi-sweep, and clipped-step counters make this work visible without timers or allocation in the solver.

decisions.title: The exact feasibility seed owns the equality factorization
decisions.detail: An Exact feasibility seed and equality-nullspace construction consume the same normalized matrix and pseudoinverse bytes, so the second decomposition is reused. A Near seed that receives active-set polish invalidates that proof and refactors. Style is terminal, so its task is solved and diagnosed but no unused lower-priority projector is constructed.

decisions.title: Canonical cold decomposition arithmetic
decisions.detail: A right-singular-basis warm start changed the 600-tick G1 contact-transfer trajectory and active-set/status sequence, so it was rejected. Revision r30 instead caches each Jacobi column's squared norm during a sweep, updates the two rotated energies algebraically, and recomputes all energies in the original summation order at every sweep boundary. The kernel matches the independent established Jacobi implementation across random, rectangular, and rank-deficient matrices within 1e-10 relative error. Tiny within-sweep ordering differences still change later active-boundary choices, so G1 behavior is deliberately reaccepted under unchanged physical and hard-row gates rather than described as trace parity.

decisions.title: Wheel-center no-slip is distinct from free tangential travel
decisions.detail: RollingPoint now means a skate/caster: forward tangent acceleration is unconstrained. RollingWheel adds the hard nonholonomic row a_center,x + c·q̈_wheel = a_command, where c is compiled from wheel radius and world wheel-axis orientation. A bounded -k·(v_center,x + c·q̇_wheel) term repairs velocity drift. The row is attached to a wheel-center frame because Upkie's tire contact virtual link is a rotating material point whose Jacobian already contains wheel spin.

decisions.title: Articulated balance observes axle-to-CoM virtual pitch
decisions.detail: The Upkie reference PI state feedback remains position error plus pitch error with an integral velocity state and wheel-velocity command. During an articulated base target, base pitch alone is insufficient because hip/knee motion moves the full-system CoM without rotating the torso. Bonesaw therefore derives virtual pitch as atan2(CoMₓ−axleₓ, CoM_z−axle_z), then lowers the reference wheel velocity to bounded wheel acceleration tasks. Python owns perturbation cases; Rust owns state-local model products, hierarchy, and effort. R130 admits one rooted sagittal external-plant recovery envelope; general contact transitions and broader robustness remain provisional.

decisions.title: World-classical floating tangent
decisions.detail: Root velocity is [angular; linear] in control_world, and root linear acceleration is the classical acceleration of the root origin. The Pinocchio oracle explicitly converts from its spatial-acceleration convention.

decisions.title: The hosted editor separates TARGET preview from physical PUSH
decisions.detail: The public 8777 deployment explicitly enables BONESAW_LIVE_GUIDED=1 for green Cartesian targets. That path slews authored XYZ intent, preserves wheel anchors through planar IK, reserves 0.25 mm over z=0, searches back along an unsafe request, and renders WBC authority without claiming realization. /plant-ws stays connected while the page is open: TARGET labels the green pose as WBC TARGET PREVIEW and overlays a dashed orange MUJOCO MEASURED rig plus contacts; PUSH makes measured transforms primary and permits a bounded ray-hit wrench on any body. Each 50 Hz stream frame contains one 50 Hz WBC tick followed by five 4 ms MuJoCo steps, and streams root motion, effort, acceleration, generalized constraint force, energy, warning, penetration, clock, capture/station/resource evidence, and R307 action witnesses. A plant disconnect ghosts state and disables physical controls. Earlier raw SE(3) self-integration remains retained experimental evidence and is used by neither mode.

decisions.title: Viewport manipulation is an explicit camera-plane contract
decisions.detail: An empty-canvas primary-pointer drag orbits a perspective camera around world Z with bounded elevation; mousewheel zooms and Shift-drag always translates the view. In TARGET mode a green point authors a world-space target on the camera-facing plane. Ctrl+drag takes precedence, ray-tests the rendered triangle surfaces, and preserves the nearest hit as the physical application point; its view-plane delta becomes an orange force arrow at 60 N/m, clamped by the server-advertised 8 N limit and refreshed every 50 ms against a 140 ms TTL. Each record declares interactive_operator source, declared_continuous_wrench class, and world force/application-point frames; the UI echoes the accepted source beside the wrench. Explicit PUSH retains a touch-friendly mode. Picking and camera state remain browser concerns; target and wrench protocols remain view-independent and distinct.

decisions.title: Editor geometry comes from the compiled robot model
decisions.detail: The WebSocket Hello record carries compiled collision and visual geometry in body-local coordinates. The browser tessellates primitives once, checksum-pinned upstream STL assets are fetched once and reduced through deterministic vertex clustering, and every surface composes with the same streamed body transforms used by frame queries. BODY and RIG are independent layers. R223 fills the exact z=0 plane, retains a 0.25 mm collision-registration margin, calculates transformed visual-vertex clearance live, and colors any face below -1 mm red. The end-to-end gate independently transforms all 41 visuals and 25 mesh instances from streamed frames; minimum measured clearance is 0.135636 mm.
